en: Table of Contents for the Recorded Sayings of Master Yun’an:
The Record of the Great Sage Puzhao Chan Monastery in Zhenjiang Prefecture.
Recorded Sayings of Baoen Guangxiao Chan Temple in Zhenzhou;
Recorded Sayings of Husheng Wanshou Chan Temple on Mount Daochang in Anji Prefecture;
Dharma Words; Eulogies on the Buddhas and Patriarchs; Verses on Ancient Cases.
The Discourse Record of Master Xingshi Yun’an during his tenure at Dashing Puzhao Chan Temple in the Prefecture of Zhenjiang,
compiled by Attendant Yuanjing.
On the eighth day of the third month in the second year of the Kaixi era, the Master accepted an invitation to enter Baohua Mountain Temple in Pingjiang Prefecture.
At the main gate, the doors and windows stood wide open; one went straight out and straight in—like a catfish climbing a bamboo pole, where even a swift hawk cannot catch up.
The Hall of Sizhou appeared in Yangzhou; sitting firmly upon Shouqiu, his heels did not touch the ground. He won only a body full of sorrow.
Were it not for an affinity of enmity, heads would not meet.
The Abbot’s quarters. Sun-face, Moon-face. A thunderclap and a flash of lightning—coming straight down! Look quickly with your eyes! Holding up the notice:
The horse’s head turns back; the ox’s head is lost. Once a single character enters the official gate, nine oxen cannot drag it out.
Holding up his robe: Such skin and hair undergo a thousand transformations and ten thousand changes. The Yellow Plum and Vulture Peak have been transmitted in vain;
whether the descendants of later generations are noble or base depends on them alone.
The Dharma seat: sitting yet not abiding, abiding yet not sitting. A drop of water forms ice; wind fans the fire.

Having ascended the seat and finished offering incense for the Emperor, he next holds up the incense and says: "This incense is both laughable and pitiable; who can I turn to to speak of this grieving heart?"
"Before Mount Yezhu, he once lost his footing; a weight of a thousand *jin* rests upon a single hair’s breadth.

Having brought forth all with full sincerity, [the assembly] makes offerings to the Great Master Songyuan, Former Abbot of Lingyin Chan Temple in Lin’an Prefecture, to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk.
Thereupon, they take their seats. Master Ganlu Nu’ān Zhao strikes the gavel and says: "In this Dharma assembly, the dragons..."
"Assembly of elephants, you should contemplate the primary truth. The Master said: "The drum has not yet sounded; I have not yet ascended this seat. What a fine model for an ancient Buddha!
Is there anyone who knows the proper time and discerns what is appropriate? A monk asked: "Shouldering the staff across my shoulder, I roam freely through tiger dens and topple the palaces of Māra.
Grasping the 'Blowing-Off-Hair' sword, I directly slay Buddhas and Patriarchs. At such a moment as this, how is it? The Master—
Yunmen said, "The cliffs have collapsed and the rocks have split. Cuiyan Jin said, "Today you have gone out for a small matter, yet you have encountered a great one.
Yunmen said, "To invite a thief and let him plunder the house. Jin asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style do you succeed?
Yunmen said, "The ass's business is not yet over when the horse's business arrives. Jin asked, "Is this not the true lineage of Dongshan, the heir to Songyuan? Yunmen said, "From here on..."
"Ten thousand miles to the Western Heaven. The monk stepped forward and asked, "Is there anything further above this?
The Master said, "One spring, two winters; hands folded across the chest. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Mazu Daoyi of Jiangxi and Huairang of Nanyue.
The monk bowed. The Master said, "Today I have lost ground. He then said: "Breaking through the azure void, the myriad phenomena..."

Level and still. A shout scatters the white clouds; ancient and modern are uniquely revealed. Fully manifesting one’s spirit and vigor, there is no room for hesitation. Fire is cast and stars fly; with a raised eye, one looks ten thousand miles away.
To investigate its direction, there is another source from which it comes. Wondrously turning in a continuous stream, it produces a truly remarkable character.
It reaches the point where the Buddhas of the three periods and the six generations of patriarchs can do nothing but blink their eyes. When one arrives here, they are pushed aside.
Neither advancing forward nor retreating backward, by whose power of grace do you receive [this state] in both the mundane and supramundane worlds? Do you understand this thoroughly?
"All quarters celebrate as they turn to the enlightened sovereign; once more we see the Yellow River clear."
Again, [the Master] cites the occasion when the King of Min invited Luoshan to ascend the hall. Luoshan adjusted his robes, looked over the assembly, and immediately descended from the seat.
The King stepped forward, took Luoshan’s hand, and said, "How does this assembly on Vulture Peak differ from today?

Luoshan replied, "I thought you were but a worldly man. The Master comments: "Dragons gallop and tigers stride; jade rolls and pearls turn. He shatters the barriers of past and present, leaving no flaw in the white jade."
There is no anvil. Although peace has been achieved through sitting, it has not yet been utterly eradicated. [The Master] strikes the whisk. To forge a sword, one must use steel from Lishui.
The white mallet proclaims: "Observe closely the Dharma of the Dharma King; the Dharma of the Dharma King is thus."
That evening’s informal discourse: Monks of our school are like dragons and tigers; amidst whirling winds and surging clouds, who can do anything to you?
Sometimes we take a single blade of grass and make it the sixteen-foot golden body; sometimes we blow a tuft of cloth-hair and transmit the True Dharma Eye.
Beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations—pure and vast, bright and clear—it penetrates directly through ten thousand layers of barriers. Not...
Abiding beyond the azure heavens, the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot lift him up; the Śakrāloka eye cannot peer into him.
When he raises a single pivot and reveals a single realm, cliffs crumble, rocks split, and the hundred rivers flow backward.

Acting as a bridge and a ferry for Buddhas and Patriarchs, serving as a model for humans and devas—if you are thus informed, is there anyone who can scrutinize this? (He strikes the meditation staff. "A team of four horses cannot overtake it."
And [the case of] the Tongue. Furthermore, he raised the public case of National Teacher Langye asking Master Fahua, "Where have you recently come from?
The Master commented: "Everyone says that Langye was attacked by Fahua’s weapons; who knows that Fahua was actually exposed by Langye?"
Nevertheless, have you not heard it said: "To see profit and forget righteousness—thus, the Way of the gentleman is rare indeed.
As I ascend the hall for the two orders of officials: wind and clouds gather, dragons and tigers gallop; advancing and retreating, each acts as is appropriate.
The monastic community flourishes, and the life of wisdom radiates its brilliance. How thick is the skin on Shouqiu’s face? Only those who are thoroughly versed in the Way are permitted [to know].
The author knows. Upon ascending the hall:
For several days since entering the monastery, there has been a clamorous bustle of human affairs; my two feet have run like smoke, and my eyes could not see my own nostrils.
When the Great Sage National Teacher heard of this, he came out and said, "How rare! Why? Because of the Lamp-Lighting One of the past.
The Buddha’s original radiance and auspicious signs are like this.
Returning from Huaidong, he ascends the hall; having returned, he goes out. Kāśyapa is poor and Ānanda is rich; going out, he returns.
South of the Heavenly Terrace, north of the Five Terraces; wrapped within the present moment, his face is covered in dust. Where the power of Yu did not reach, the sound of the river flows on.
[The Master] turned toward the west.
Entering the hall, he raised the verse on Lingyun’s realization upon seeing peach blossoms. Xuansha said, "It is indeed true, most truly true;

yet I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate. The Master said, "In the same pit, there is no difference in the soil; there are certainly those who are distant and those who are close."
Incense is offered on the anniversary of the passing of my late teacher, Songyuan. To approach him is to be presumptuous; to distance oneself from him is likewise so.
He is without principle and without sentiment; he is both noble and base. Year after year, the snow deepens his grievance; in the end, no one has attained the authentic transmission.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Tathāgatas of the past have already perfected this gate; with a single blow of the mallet, it is shattered.
The Bodhisattvas of the present each now enter perfect luminosity; wind and fire seethe together. Those who practice and study in the future should abide in accordance with this."
"The tongue is pressed against the upper palate. When Shouqiu spoke thus, he was merely providing a ladder for the thief.
When Master Langye Menggu arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "An old friend has come from beyond the secular world; upon meeting, we understand each other at once.
Counting back thirty years, our path of righteousness was established on the same day. Iron walls and silver mountains—utterly in ruins! It reaches the point of being identical."
"Like sounds responding to one another, and like those of the same nature seeking each other out. Master Shizi of Xihe was at Fenzhou.
He ascended the hall and, citing a case involving Caoshan, said: "A monk once asked Caoshan, 'The tax collector is poor and destitute;

I beg the Master for relief. Caoshan called out, 'Tax Collector! The monk responded, 'Yes? Caoshan said, 'At Qingyuan’s house, they drink three cups of wine and yet still say they have not been touched by it.'"
"His lips. The Master said, "Using poison to counteract poison; using a wedge to drive out a wedge. Old Cao Shan does not recognize it;
where is this monk’s place for drinking wine?
*Recorded Sayings of Baoen Guangxiao Chan Temple in Zhenzhou*
Attendant Zhìnéng compiled this selection of slips to ensure that no action is taken in vain and no arrow is shot in vain. Should one hesitate, then two nines are eighteen.
On the first day of the new year, he ascended the hall. He cited a monk who asked Jingqing, "Is there still Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year?
Jingqing said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma of the new year? Jingqing said, "The first month of the year begins its reign;
all things are renewed. The monk said, "Thank you, Master, for your answer. Jingqing said, "Jingqing has lost out. Another monk asked Mingjiao about the new year.
[The Master] asked, "Is there still Buddha-dharma at the head? The scripture says, "There is not. The monk said, "Year after year is a good year;
day after day is a good day. Why then is it 'not'? The scripture says, "When Mr. Zhang drinks wine, Mr. Li gets drunk.

The monk said, "Old and decrepit as you are, you have a dragon's head but a snake's tail. The scripture says, "Today he has lost ground. The Master commented, "Existence and non-existence are not matters of intention."
This is a matter of vital energy. Both Mingjiao and Jingqing lost their advantage. When someone asked Baolin, "Is there still Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year?
he took up his staff and struck him. Why? Because, in every case, one must not interpret this through the perspective of a wild fox spirit.
Ascending the hall, Huangbo addressed the assembly, saying: "All of you here are nothing but fellows who eat nothing but dregs of wine.
Having presented the public case, he added: "The gate of the cavern has no lock; the Sword Pass is steep and lofty. The wind and dew are high and cold;
this is certainly not the world of men. This is so, yet how many among heaven and earth know it? This monk failed to bring forth an answer to a single question; Huangbo was present in his very being.
This is mud and water.
On the first day of winter, he ascends the hall, plants his staff upright, and says: "The Yang has begun to rise. A pair of fish startle from the treetops;
long bamboo shoots burst forth from the rocks. Leaning on his staff, he says: "On this day, I respectfully wish that the high-ranking members of both orders and those present here may be well."

The pure assembly has arrived. On this day of the longest night, may you doubly receive blessings and prosperity. (He lets out a shout. "Vulgar habits have not yet been eliminated. Ascending the hall:
As the late spring gradually warms, birds sing and flowers bloom in numbers as vast as the sands of the Ganges; seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are all perfectly clear.
Why, then, were the old, frozen sores of India turned about by sounds and forms, causing their descendants in later generations to...
Each and every one of them cannot lift their feet. Tell me, where does the point of benefit and harm lie? Though gold dust is precious, when it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "When a single leaf falls, autumn comes to the world; when a single speck of dust rises, the great earth is gathered up. Linji struck Huangbo with his palm. Nan...
Quán calls out to Zhāozhōu: "The opening of the mouth is not upon the tongue. The night tide urges the departure of the ship for Hǎinán.
Compiled by the attendant Wéiyǎn from the *Recorded Sayings* of Hùshèng Wànshòu Chán Temple on Dàocháng Mountain in Ānjìng Prefecture.
Ascending the hall: The dragon roars and the tiger howls; the Dipper turns and the stars shift. Eradicating the customs of antiquity, he opens up the essential pivot of the present age.
The commands of the Dharma-society issue spontaneously; these refined teachings may be renewed daily. With a single movement of the head of the hall, how does one strike and sing?
A wondrous dance requires no boastful display of rhythmic changes; the three stages must be urged forward by all together.

Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: When Linji entered the capital to propagate the Dharma, he arrived at the gate of a certain household and said, "I am here to supplement my bowl with your family's provisions.
The old woman said, "You are truly insatiable! Linji replied, "I have not even received any rice; why do you say I am insatiable?
The woman then shut the door. The Master commented: "To 'supplement the bowl'—Linji was buried alive on level ground. 'Truly insatiable'—the old woman."
When a person dies, one does not offer condolences.

[The Master] ascends the hall. He cites Shishuang Ciming, who would sometimes, within his quarters, place a basin of water, upon it a single-bladed sword, and beneath that a pair of straw sandals, with a staff resting horizontally across his knees. When a monk entered the door, he would simply point at them.
As he was about to raise his staff, the Master held it up and said: "A clever smile; a beautiful glance; using the plain as the brilliant.

Then, Master Chinoan arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "The Patriarch Xianci and my Dharma brother Nuonan—whose spiritual power is like a flash of lightning and whose eloquence is like a rushing river—they met by chance without intent, yet they became objects of mutual resentment. Neither could stand the other."
Planting Grass. The Way of our late Master has become increasingly precarious. Entering the hall:
Last night at the third watch, while in a dream, I was blown by a gale of black wind into the realm of rākṣasa demons;
my life was nearly lost. Fortunately, the morning bell struck once, startling me awake. Opening my eyes... [I see that it was but a dream.]
The eyes have a thousand heads and a hundred threads; they bring trouble upon the patriarchs Hu Da Mo and Śākyamuni.
The lacquered bucket is set aside, yet the head monk in the hall lacks not even a single fraction of it. Why? Benevolence and righteousness are entirely severed at the place of poverty;
worldly sentiment leans exclusively toward those with wealth.
Incense is offered at the stupa of my late teacher Songyuan. He severed the orthodox lineage of Yangqi and shattered the steel-like school of Linji.
Red earth was smeared upon the udder of a cow; the secret chamber remained airless. With matters unresolved before and after his physical presence, he is buried deep within the white clouds.
Neither father nor son, they meet by chance along the road; the pond-weeds and stream-cress are left behind in neglect. Master Xie mistook it for a fishing boat.
[He] ascended the hall and cited Zifu’s instruction to the assembly: "Seeing the monastery flagpole of Zifu from across the river, one turns back immediately—at the very base of one's heels."
"He would have received thirty blows; how much more so for one who has come across the river! At that moment, a monk just stepped out. Fokuang said, "He is not fit to converse with.
The Master commented: "To incite a thief to plunder his own house."
When Master Lingyin Shigu arrived, he was invited to ascend the hall. The Master led the assembly, saying:

"Within the School of the Patriarchs, there are one thousand seven hundred cases known as 'ancient precedents. They are also called 'superfluous things. To pick them up is to defile one's lips and teeth."
Set this aside for a moment. Each monk has his own koan: the fences have collapsed, the walls have fallen, the ravines are blocked, and the ditches are filled;
it is truly impossible to prop them up. One does not understand by asking the Buddha; one does not understand by asking the Patriarchs;
one does not understand by asking the late Great White Useless Uncle; and one does not understand by asking the late Master Songyuan of Lingyin. It is no different at Daochang.
Meeting. It is my good fortune that my Dharma-uncle Shigong has graced this mountain with a visit.

He will surely untangle our attachments and remove our bonds, pull out the nails and extract the wedges, so that I, your junior nephew, and the entire assembly may attain a state of peace and happiness. As it is said: "One for East, two for Winter; hands folded at the chest;

going downhill without running—such a swift opportunity is hard to encounter. [The assembly] descends from their seats together to offer their prostrations, entreating him to grant us his instruction. Please deign to open the way for us.

[The Master] showed [the incense]. On the anniversary of the passing of Founding Master Fuhu, he held up the incense and said: "Old Nü dies this morning; Old Yan is born this day. Both lack any skill or artifice;

though they share a dream, they do not sleep on the same bed. By fortunate coincidence, we follow one another’s footsteps, yet the incense and lamps have grown desolate. My very entrails [are moved]."
Even iron must be forged; how can donkey dung be compared to musk?

On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "One lamp kindles hundreds of thousands of lamps; lamp after lamp is inexhaustible. I wonder from where this one lamp comes forth?
He struck his staff on the ground and said, "For now, it does not come from here. After a long silence, he said: "The bamboo staff transforms into a dragon."
"Go! You foolish man, you are like one bailing out a night pond. Entering the hall, [the Master said:
"To disparage the Buddha and slander the Dharma, not to be counted among the assembly—what kind of person is this? This is a human site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).
His innate nature is so biased and narrow that it simply cannot be contained; yet, we cannot help but provide him with his rightful portion of fodder. We shall banish him to another world-system."
In the midst of the cold ground, there is a moment of sudden awakening; one will never fail the old monk.
During a winter night, he raised the kōan concerning Dongshan and Head Seat Tai eating fruit. The Master said, "Old Dongshan disgraced the ancestral wind;
Head Seat Tai buried his own self. Together they embroidered a pair of mandarin ducks, sustaining [the Dharma] through the ages."
[The incense does] not arise.
On the anniversary of Chan Master Fuhu’s passing, he offered incense. In the fourth year, he assumed his duties at Yunfeng Temple. "In vain I write of autumnal sorrows;
to whom shall they be sent? Every year on the fifth day of the eleventh month, because one doubt was resolved only for another doubt to arise, I [re-established] the founding of the mountain.

Chan Master Fu Hu pointed at the willow and cursed the poplar; he pitied the tortoise while excusing the soft-shelled turtle. You die and I live—do not speak of a bowl of coarse tea or a single stick of incense;
even that would be better than reconciling with the blind and suing the blind.

A Small Sermon on New Year’s Eve: The pivot that not a thousand sages have transmitted fills the ditches and blocks the ravines; the phrase that a monk cannot utter has horns upon its head and carries it aloft. When the year ends and the age is spent, one’s life is like a thread hanging from a string; when the twelfth month concludes and spring returns, the stone man claps his hands. Thus and so, when the Dharma emerges, the crafty arise; not thus and not so, Xu Liu carries the wooden board. As it is said: "If you meet a Buddha, kill the Buddha; if you meet a patriarch, kill the patriarch. If you can act like this, you will see the old master of the temple hall laughing heartily. If you cannot, then go and ask the stone man for the answer. Go! Go! Do not tarry! Do not tarry! If you do not understand, then listen to the verse: "The Great Matter is not something to be sought far away; It is right here, before your very eyes. When the snow melts and the ice breaks, The spring wind blows through the ten directions. Do not seek it in the scriptures or the commentaries; Do not look for it in the words of the ancients. If you can let go of all contrivances, Then the whole world is the Way. Go! Go! Do not tarry! Do not tarry! If you still do not understand, then come forward and ask me. If you can speak a word, I shall give you a staff; if you cannot, I shall strike you with my whisk. Do not hesitate! Do not hesitate! If you hesitate, you will fall into the pit of birth and death. Go! Go! Do not tarry! Do not tarry! If you can act like this, you will see the old master of the temple hall laughing heartily. If you cannot, then go and ask the stone man for the answer. Go! Go! This is the report. It is neither a deliberation on the Buddha-dharma nor a conventional worldly discourse.
As for the old king of the eastern village burning paper money at night—how would you explain that? (He lets out a shout.)
Again, he raised the koan of Deshan’s “Small Lecture on Not Answering Questions. The Master commented: "Throughout his life, Deshan relied upon a single white staff;
he would strike even if a Buddha came, and he would strike even if an Ancestor came. Yet, for no reason, he harbored doubt before this monk."
This has caused him to be scrutinized by others for all eternity. Is there anyone tonight who can save Deshan?
[He] threw down his staff.
On the anniversary of the passing of my late teacher Songyuan, I offer this incense: "Short-necked and deaf, a thousand demons and a hundred monsters. Thus, thirty [years].
Year. Continuing the true lineage of Dongshan. I too have deliberated wrongly. Three prostrations and one incense burner—let others at their leisure speak of its merits or flaws.
Dharma Words.
To the Chan practitioner Shoude:
The Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is like the great sun-disk; it rises in the void, illuminating everything without exception.

It is only because emotions arise that wisdom is obstructed, and because conceptualizations shift that the essence becomes alienated. Thus, our Teacher with the Yellow Face labored for forty-nine years, speaking here and there in the East.

It was said: at the very end, he held up a flower and smiled. From that time until now, throughout India and this land, the patriarchs have successively joined in the fragrance of the flower and the lamps have divided their flames, none of whom failed to uphold this very matter.
It is not that they did not penetrate to the very top and bottom; it was cutting through iron and chopping through nails. One might say:
"A blind man leading a crowd of blind men, pulling one another into a pit of fire. Yet, if there were a person who could kill the Buddhas and kill the patriarchs, then—
Raising dust against the wind, surging through crashing waves; roaming Mount Luofu in the morning and returning to Mount Tante in the evening.

Trapped in a cage yet refusing to stay; called out to, yet turning no head. Moving in and out with unimpeded mastery through the realms of Buddhas and demons, amidst mountains of knives and masses of fire.
He extinguishes the orthodox lineage of Linji and blinds the treasury of the True Dharma Eye. Such is his resolve.
To establish oneself in this manner, to leave home and travel on foot in this manner, and to uphold the true command in this manner—this only saves half the matter.
Moreover, if one is bitten three times or twice and still cannot sever the connection, one will, as before, be cast back into the bag of old junk.
Not only do you bury yourself, but you also neglect the teachings of the former patriarchs. Do not blame me for my many words at Shouqiu;
you are simply judging from a cold, detached perspective.

The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yun’an (Concluded):
A Biographical Account of Chan Master Yun’an of Husheng Wansui Chan Temple on Mount Daochang in Anji Prefecture,
the Flourishing Song Dynasty.
The Master’s name was Puyan; his courtesy name was Shaohan. He was born in the twenty-sixth year of the Shaoxing era (1156), a *bingzi* year, into the Du family of Siming.
Upon reaching maturity, he remained detached from the world and refused to bow his head in submission to worldly conventions; he quickly underwent tonsure and ordination.
Initially, together with Yigong of Shigu, he visited Wuyong Quan and various other venerable elders.

In the first month of the spring of the Jiachen year, the eleventh year of the Chunxi era of Emperor Xiaozong, Chan Master Songyuan Yue appeared in the world at Chengzhao Monastery in Pingjiang to propagate the Way of Mian Shanqing.
His disciples washed their bowls and sought instruction with diligent persistence; at that time, the Master was thirty years of age.
Before long, Songyuan moved to Guangxiao in Jiangyin and then to Yuyang at Yufu in Wuyue, and the Master followed him into his quarters in both instances.
In the midst of this, he was exalted. Water and milk blended together; he appointed the Master to serve at Mount Xiangshan.
In the ninth month of autumn in the first year of the Shaohui era of Emperor Guangzong, the gengxu year, Dong Rao invited the Master to Juefu Temple to lead the assembly.
Upon relinquishing his post and returning to Jin, Songyuan presented him with a verse as a parting gift: "The courtyard of Yezhu is desolate; the winds and waves of East Lake are turbulent."

Alas! How many people can truly know the mind? Like a solitary osprey in the autumn sky across ten thousand miles, Songyuan led Mingzhe through eight assemblies at Xiangshan, Huqiu in Suzhou, and Lingyin and Baoci in Hangzhou.
For eighteen years, they followed one another like a form and its shadow.
His profound and subtle [wisdom] was utterly refined. He once sat on the same seat as [Master Lingyin] to receive disciples. For the sake of his mother, he returned to his hometown at Beijian;
when Master Jian composed a long verse to console him upon his departure, the monastic community has recited it to this day.

In the eighth month of the autumn of the second year of Jia Tai (Renjia) of Emperor Ningzong’s reign, Songyuan was about to pass away; he presented the Dharma robe of Chan Master Baiyun Yuan, which had been transmitted to him, once again.
The top-knot image (uṣṇīṣa) was bestowed upon him. The Master removed his robe and received the image; he then requested his uncle, Master Pò'ān, to compose a eulogy for it.
